newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus bourse market cap down 1.8 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bourse market cap down 1.8 pct in July.

text.p: The market capitalisation of the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) fell 1.8 percent to 1.142 billion pounds ($2.08 billion) in July from the previous month, according to bourse figures released on Wednesday.
The market capitalisation of the exchange, which trades in 88 securities from 45 listed companies, was 1.163 million pounds in June.
A monthly report issued by the CSE said the banking sector accounted for 55.34 percent of total market capitalisation, the manufacturing sector 10.83 percent and the insurance sector 7.29 percent.
The trading sector represented 3.74 percent, the tourism sector 4.89 percent, miscellaneous companies 4.12 percent and approved investment companies 2.34 percent.
The share of corporate bonds on the market was 7.52 percent and that of government bonds 2.93 percent.
The total value of transactions during July reached 10.3 million pounds with an average of 447,000 per trading session.
The banking sector contributed 46.02 percent of the total value traded, which was the highest, while government bonds had the lowest contribution at 0.37 percent.

Hot stocks during July were shares in the Bank of Cyprus (Holdings) Ltd which accounted for 28.92 percent of the total volume traded followed by shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank Ltd with a 21.01 percent share and the Hellenic Bank Ltd with 7.80 percent.

The highest level that the General Price Index reached during July was 76.70 points and the lowest 74.31 points. On a sectoral level, the trading companies sector showed the highest decrease of 10.11 percent, followed by insurance companies with 8.58 percent and manufacturing companies with a 7.07 percent drop.

A bourse official told Reuters on Wednesday that by the end of August the number of companies listed on the exchange will increase by two to 47, from the listing of Dodonis Investments Company and Options Eurocongress, a firm specialising in organising medical conferences in Cyprus and abroad. ($=0.547 Cyprus pounds)
